title: Wire onError (and a recovery-pull path) into TutoredListenerSupervisor's inner ListenerSupervisor

evidence.quote:
onError: (Object error, StackTrace stackTrace) {
          _onError?.call(channel, error, stackTrace);

why: TutoredListenerSupervisor.attach() builds its ListenerSupervisor with only `source` and `onEvent` -- no `onError`, no `recoveryPullTriggers`. Inside ListenerSupervisor.start(), a stream error calls `_onError?.call(...)`, which is a silent no-op when `_onError` is null. Firestore terminates a `.snapshots()` stream on error (e.g. permission-denied when a parent revokes the grant while the tutor's 15 tutored channels are live, or any transient stream fault) -- so that one channel goes permanently dark for the rest of the session, with zero AppLogger entry, zero Crashlytics record, and no resubscription, while sibling channels keep working. The parallel own-profile path in sync_orchestrator.dart wires `onError: _onListenerError` (logs, forwards to Crashlytics, fires analytics) and `recoveryPullTriggers` (recovers from at-limit snapshots) -- the tutored path has neither, so it is both less observable and less self-healing than the path it was copied from.
recommendation: Pass `onError` (log via AppLogger at minimum, consider triggering TutoredPullService.pull() on permission-denied) and `recoveryPullTriggers` into the ListenerSupervisor built in TutoredListenerSupervisor.attach(), mirroring SyncOrchestratorImpl.start().
acceptance_criteria: Unit test: a ListenerSource stub that emits a stream error during an attached tutored session asserts the error reaches a logger/callback, not silently dropped.
TutoredListenerSupervisor.attach() passes a non-null onError to ListenerSupervisor(...).

corrections: Finding cites tutored_listener_supervisor.dart:97 for the 'source: source' line; actual file has '_supervisor = ListenerSupervisor(' at line 97 and 'source: source,' at line 98 -- one-line offset, immaterial to the claim.
